Hi Dana — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the SOW.

High level: we typically present three commercial paths depending on customer preference for capex vs opex and control over keys:

- Seat-based HSM (reserved): one-time implementation + monthly seat fee per HSM partition. Best if you want fixed-cost amortization and predictable capacity.
- Throughput (metered): per-1000-ops model for HSM usage. Lower upfront but variable month-to-month.
- Blended bands: throughput tiers with a sliding-fee cap and a reduced seat fee for a smaller committed pool.

I'm attaching a simple concession matrix that shows the econ for those three paths with example usage bands and two concession levers: early-adopter credit (applied as a one-time implementation credit) and a volume-tier discount for committed annual throughput.

On SOC2 and audit logs: we can provide an extract of our SOC2 report and a sanitized snapshot of audit-log retention. For Mediwell's EU/US residency split we can:
- Ship audit logs daily to your S3 bucket (encrypted-in-transit).
- Configure retention windows (30/90/365) per dataset; longer retention adds storage/processing fees shown in the matrix.

Looping in Ben (solutions) and Kimberly (enterprise) to confirm the capacity assumptions and whether legal is comfortable with the proposed credit structure.

Next steps: Ben, can you confirm the latency/throughput impact of a blended model for the usage bands below? Kimberly — I'll need an approval range for an early-adopter concession we can offer (one-time credit or x% off for first N months).

Thanks — attaching: Redwood_Concession_Matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi all — quick technical notes to support the matrix.

1) HSM scaling profile: a single HSM partition (logical seat) can handle sustained cryptographic operations up to ~250 rps for signing/unwrap workloads we typically see in inference key unwraps; beyond that you either shard across partitions (adds seat cost) or move to throughput metering where we amortize GPU-bound ops differently.

2) Latency impact: the blended band approach keeps average 95th-percentile latency within our SLA if we reserve at least 1.25x capacity headroom for the 100k-1M band. If you intend to burst beyond 1M frequently, the seat model with autoscale buffer is safer for latency.

3) Audit export: daily export to your S3 is straightforward — we produce gzipped, signed JSON files. For EU residency we can direct those exports to an EU bucket; note that cross-region replication will add a small cost (~0.5% of monthly HSM cost in our model).

I'm attaching an HSM capacity estimate worksheet with a couple of sample usage profiles (low/med/high) so the economic rows in Jordan's matrix can be tuned.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the detail. From a commercial/legal standpoint I can approve the following offer to present to MediWell procurement:

1) Commitment & credit: a 12-month reserved capacity commitment qualifies for a one-time implementation credit equal to 3 months of the monthly seat fee (applied as a credit on the first invoice). Alternatively, if MediWell prefers throughput billing, we will apply a 10% early-adopter discount to the first 3 months of metered throughput charges.

2) Volume discounting: an additional staged volume discount for throughput tiers (5% at >250k calls/mo, 12% at >750k calls/mo, 18% at >1.5M calls/mo) as shown in Jordan's matrix. All discounts subject to a 12-month minimum term.

3) Evidence delivery: SOC2 snapshot and a sanitized audit-log retention sample will be delivered within 5 business days of signature. Daily S3 export to your bucket is supported; we will provide the export manifest and a pointer to the retention lifecycle config.

4) Contract mechanics: if this is acceptable, I'll push a term sheet and prepare a DocuSign envelope (we prefer a 12-month initial term with automatic renewal). Please confirm the preferred concession option (seat-credit vs throughput-discount) and whether the PO will reference DEAL-9843.

Jordan — please attach the final concession matrix with the seat vs throughput rows tuned to the sample profiles Ben provided; Dana — attaching the SOC2 snapshot and the concession matrix will be helpful for your procurement review.
